title: Asymmetric tenant stress mitigation and rapid prime playbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: During a high-traffic window two tenants generated asymmetric spike patterns that saturated a subset of GPU pools, causing multi-minute queue buildup, token throttling, and tail-latency regressions for hosted API customers. This ticket captures the actionable follow-ups, owners, and acceptance criteria to prevent recurrence by combining rapid-prime automation, tenant-aware admission, and better telemetry for signal routing.

What happened: A mix of long-sequence requests from Tenant A (large batched chat sessions) combined with a sudden burst of short inference traffic from Tenant B. Autoscaler priming lag + suboptimal admission scoring allowed the long-sequence workload to monopolize prewarmed slots and KV cache locality, amplifying queue length on specific shards. Reactive throttles kicked in inconsistently which created oscillation and poor p99 latency for unaffected tenants.

High-level mitigation goals: 1) reduce single-tenant queue amplification on a shard, 2) ensure fast recovery of effective throughput via rapid priming, 3) add tenant-aware admission scoring to protect fair share, 4) provide clear playbooks and dashboards for on-call runbook steps.
action_items: Automate rapid-prime: implement a targeted prewarm pipeline that runs a lightweight model-weight pin + small probe workload to reduce cold-starts on warmed pools (owner: Jordan Kim, due: 2025-02-11, estimate: 3)

Tenant-aware admission score: extend admission scorer to include recent token-rate and sequence-length histograms per tenant; cap continuous-slot-ownership at configurable percent (owner: Priya Desai, due: 2025-02-14, estimate: 5)

Adaptive short-window shedder: add short-window (30s) shedding policy that favors shorter seq-length requests under queue pressure to improve overall throughput (owner: Malik Thompson, due: 2025-02-10, estimate: 3)
KV-locality eviction policy: implement best-effort KV cache preemption signals for low-value long-seq tenants when pool is congested (owner: Elena Rossi, due: 2025-02-18, estimate: 5)

Coordinated autoscaler priming: change autoscaler to trigger opportunistic small-scale priming (1-2 nodes) when allocation signals predict imminent demand within 2 minutes (owner: Yuki Tanaka, due: 2025-02-12, estimate: 3)

Dashboard & alerting: add new multi-tenant shard view showing per-tenant queue depth, mean sequence length, and admission score; create alert for shard queue growth > 75% sustained for 120s (owner: SRE Team, due: 2025-02-07, estimate: 2)

Playbook update: write explicit runbook steps for on-call to identify asymmetric tenant sources, apply targeted soft-throttle, and trigger rapid-prime (owner: Sofia Martinez, due: 2025-02-06, estimate: 1)
Post-deploy chaos run: run controlled chaos/traffic replay with synthetic asymmetric tenants to validate behavior and fix regressions (owner: QA, due: 2025-02-20, estimate: 3)
acceptance_criteria: Per-shard p99 tail latency under comparable load improves by >= 30% in asymmetric stress tests
Sustained shard queue depth under mixed-tenancy replay is reduced to < 30% of observed peak within 90s of priming
New dashboard surfaces per-tenant admission score and sequence-length histogram; alerts fire for sustained queue growth
Runbook validated in tabletop and one on-call practical exercise
No customer-facing throttling alerts triggered in the monitored canary region for 14 days post-release
postmortem_summary:
Root causes: (1) autoscaler priming was conservative and not targeted at shards under pressure; (2) admission scoring lacked tenant sequence-length awareness; (3) KV cache ownership allowed prolonged monopolization by long-sequence workloads. Contributing factors included insufficient telemetry granularity and runbook ambiguity for rapidly identifying tenant sources.

Decision rationale: Prefer a combination of short-term mitigations (rapid-prime, short-window shedding) plus medium-term improvements (tenant-aware admission, KV eviction signals). We chose not to globally lower admission thresholds because that would harm throughput for latency-sensitive short requests.

Risks: Complex admission changes could introduce fairness regressions; will mitigate via staged rollout and canary tests. KV eviction introduces risk of slightly higher token cost for rework; we accept this tradeoff to protect latency SLOs.
